lens: Naming adherence — doctrine reviewer_id format, debate-artifact filename conventions, FixupTask ID conventions, intra-repo precedent consistency
answer: PR #17 introduces a NEW naming scheme that diverges from the established doctrine precedent on TWO axes, with one drift being a doctrine-grade BLOCKER and the other a soft inconsistency. (1) reviewer_id format: pr-17 uses `codex-F<n>-pr-<N>-r<round>` (e.g. `codex-F1-pr-1-r1`, `claude-F2_hyperscaler-pr-17` for the pr-17 self-review). The doctrine reviewer_id contract per [[feedback_multispectrum_review_v22]] / [[feedback_multispectrum_adherence_facets]] is `<tool>-<facet_id>-<change_id>` where facet_id is the FULL facet name including descriptor — verified against the reference batch evidence/debate/M02-P06-FOUNDRY-SUPERVISOR-2026-05-15-F1_linus-r1.json whose reviewer_id is `claude-critic-F1_linus-M02-P06-FOUNDRY-SUPERVISOR-2026-05-15`. PR #17's wave drops the descriptor suffix (`F1` instead of `F1_linus`, `F5` instead of `F5_quality`, `F7` instead of `F7_security`) for the pr-1..pr-11 backfill artifacts, while INCONSISTENTLY using full `F2_hyperscaler` in pr-17-F2-r1.json. Same wave, two conventions. (2) Filename scheme: doctrine precedent is `<change_id>-<facet_id>-r<n>.json` (e.g. `...-F1_linus-r1.json`). PR #17 wave uses `pr-<N>-F<n>-r<round>.json` (id-only). Filename and reviewer_id are co-drift. (3) FixupTask IDs `F-PR<N>-NN` (e.g. F-PR17-01): no prior `F-PR*` precedent existed in registries/cross-cutting/fixuptasks.jsonl before this PR (verified: 4 F-PR* rows total post-merge, all from the wave; zero pre-existing). The format itself is internally consistent (zero-pad-2, hyphen-separated, PR-scoped) and the PR body §Naming justification declares the convention explicitly. ACCEPTABLE as a new naming pattern, but the doctrine reviewer_id divergence is the primary A1 drift. Verdict: request_changes.
key_claims: Doctrine reviewer_id precedent (M02-P06-FOUNDRY-SUPERVISOR-2026-05-15 reference batch) uses `<tool>-<role>-<facet_id_with_descriptor>-<change_id>` form: `claude-critic-F1_linus-M02-P06-FOUNDRY-SUPERVISOR-2026-05-15` — facet_id ALWAYS carries the descriptor name (F1_linus, F5_quality, F7_security).

PR #17 pr-1..pr-11 backfill wave uses `codex-F<n>-pr-<N>-r<round>` — descriptor suffix STRIPPED. Example from diff: `codex-F1-pr-1-r1`. This is doctrine drift on the canonical reviewer_id field, the primary uniqueness/audit anchor.

PR #17 pr-17 SELF-review files use the full descriptor: pr-17-F2-r1.json reviewer_id is `claude-F2_hyperscaler-pr-17`, pr-17-A1-r1.json (this file) is `claude-A1_naming_adherence-pr-17`. Same wave, two conventions — intra-wave inconsistency.

Filename scheme `pr-<N>-F<n>-r<round>.json` (id-only) co-drifts with the reviewer_id pattern: doctrine precedent `M02-P06-...-F1_linus-r1.json` includes the descriptor in BOTH reviewer_id and filename. PR #17 strips it in both for pr-1..pr-11.

FixupTask ID format `F-PR<N>-NN` is internally consistent (zero-pad-2 sequence, hyphen-separated, PR-scoped) and explicitly declared in PR #17 body §Naming justification — acceptable as a new convention since no prior F-PR* rows existed in registries/cross-cutting/fixuptasks.jsonl (verified: 4 total rows post-merge, all from this wave).

Per [[feedback_naming_justification]] every new name needs a one-line BNF/12-layer-enum conformance proof at scaffold time. PR #17 body provides justifications for filename + FixupTask formats but does NOT justify the reviewer_id descriptor-stripping vs doctrine precedent.

Filename pr-5-F5-r2.json without a pr-5-F5-r1.json sibling (per PR body: 'required PR #5 F5 re-dispatch round') is explicitly noted in the naming-justification block; consistent and pre-declared, not a drift.

tool prefix `codex` (pr-1..pr-11) vs `claude` (pr-17 self-review) is consistent with the actual generator topology and matches [[feedback_consensus_debate_spectrum_lens_subagents]] (separate subagents per facet); the tool token rotation is acceptable per the `<tool>-...` doctrine slot.
uncertainty_areas: Whether the descriptor-stripping was an intentional v2.3.0 spec change (PR #17 declares spec_version 2.3.0 in audit-chain payload) or an accidental shortening — no spec-diff artifact found in repo to confirm.
Whether existing tooling (omc msr, lane validators) consumes reviewer_id by exact-match on `F<n>_<descriptor>` substring; if so, the pr-1..pr-11 wave is silently un-queryable by descriptor.
Whether `F-PR<N>-NN` IDs should be padded to 3 digits at scale (next 20-PR catch-up wave with 10 fixups per PR would still fit 2 digits, so 2-pad is adequate for the foreseeable window).

findings.summary: reviewer_id descriptor-stripping in pr-1..pr-11 backfill (`codex-F1-pr-1-r1` vs doctrine precedent `claude-critic-F1_linus-M02-P06-FOUNDRY-SUPERVISOR-2026-05-15`). Same-wave inconsistency: pr-17 self-review artifacts (pr-17-F2-r1.json) DO carry the descriptor (`claude-F2_hyperscaler-pr-17`). One wave, two reviewer_id conventions = audit-query brittleness; any consumer grepping for `F1_linus` will miss 90% of the wave.
findings.recommended_action: Either (a) rewrite pr-1..pr-11 reviewer_id fields in a follow-up PR to include the descriptor (`codex-F1_linus-pr-1-r1`, etc.) to match doctrine precedent + the pr-17 self-review subset, OR (b) emit an ADR explicitly retiring the descriptor suffix in v2.3.0+ AND rewrite the pr-17 self-review reviewer_ids to match the stripped form (`claude-A1-pr-17` instead of `claude-A1_naming_adherence-pr-17`). Pick one form, apply it uniformly. The current state is the worst of both worlds.

findings.summary: Filename scheme `pr-<N>-F<n>-r<round>.json` co-drifts: doctrine reference uses `...-F1_linus-r1.json` (descriptor in filename). The id-only form makes `ls evidence/debate/ | grep linus` fail for the entire pr-1..pr-11 backfill wave. Same wave inconsistency as reviewer_id: 74 backfill files use id-only, 5 pr-17 self-review files also use id-only (so filename is internally consistent within the wave, but inconsistent with the M02-P06 doctrine reference batch).
findings.recommended_action: If the descriptor-stripping is accepted as v2.3.0 doctrine (per finding 1 path b), backfill an ADR documenting the filename convention change and add a one-time migration of evidence/debate/M02-P06-*-r1.json filenames OR an explicit grandfathered-exception note. If rejected (path a), rename the 74 backfill files to include the descriptor: `pr-1-F1_linus-r1.json` etc. — git mv preserves history.

findings.summary: PR #17 §Naming justification block declares the filename + FixupTask formats but does NOT cite the doctrine precedent (M02-P06 reference batch) or justify the reviewer_id descriptor-stripping. Per [[feedback_naming_justification]] every new name needs a one-line BNF/precedent conformance proof at scaffold time.
findings.recommended_action: Append a one-line clause to PR #17 §Naming justification (or to the ADR that resolves finding 1): 'reviewer_id format `<tool>-F<n>-<change>-r<round>` retires the descriptor suffix used by M02-P06 batch on the basis that facet_id is unique without descriptor and consumers query by integer index.' If that claim is false, fix the format instead.

findings.summary: FixupTask ID `F-PR<N>-NN` is a brand-new prefix family with no prior F-PR* rows in registries/cross-cutting/fixuptasks.jsonl. Internally consistent and declared, but the registry-naming precedent for non-PR fixuptasks (verified: 4 existing rows pre-PR-17 wave) was not surveyed in §Naming justification.
findings.recommended_action: No fix required for this PR. In a follow-up, document the F-* family taxonomy (F-PR<N>-NN for PR-derived, F-<change_id>-NN for slice/milestone-derived) in docs/standards/ so future fixuptask IDs do not collide.
